descriptions.ubi189_data_source_artifacts_2026_08_26: UBI-189 follow-up: depth-0 (top-level, always-visible-without-a-click) field descriptions for all 4526 AWS data sources. 19603 missing field instances filled, 100% of the real gap, out of 22123 total depth-0 fields (5888 distinct missing field names, by far the largest and most fragmented vocabulary of any provider in this phase). Coverage came in three tiers: an explicit, frequency-prioritized dictionary of high-frequency generic AWS API terms (next_token, max_results, resource_arn, filters, tags, and similar; the top 2 names alone -- next_token and max_results -- account for over 20% of all missing instances); a broadened set of suffix-based fallback rules (_id, _arn, _name, _type, _status, _time, and roughly 80 more suffixes) covering the many compositional <domain>_<suffix> identifier fields AWS's API surface generates; and, for the remaining ~2289 distinct names not covered by either (mostly count-1 singletons), individual hand-authored entries verified against real AWS product knowledge. Depth 1+ deliberately out of scope, same reasoning as Kubernetes, GitHub, Datadog, and Azure: every <Expandable> renders collapsed by default. Keyed data_<wire>.<field>, verified zero collisions against 30144 pre-existing entries and zero corruption of pre-existing content.

intros.ubi189_data_source_artifacts_2026_08_26: UBI-189 follow-up: data source artifact authoring, AWS after Kubernetes, GitHub, Datadog, and Azure -- the final and largest provider (4526 data sources, larger than the other five combined). 4526/4526 AWS data sources now have a real intro, keyed data_<wire>. AWS's CFN-vs-Smithy naming divergence was verified live before trusting any matching heuristic, per standing instruction: AWS data source directories/local slugs derive from Smithy service IDs while AWS resource page basenames derive from CFN's own typeName convention with no consistent, learnable prefix-stripping rule across services (unlike Azure, where stripping the service_dir worked universally) -- confirmed worse than every other provider, exactly as flagged before starting. A token-overlap sibling matcher was built and independently verified rather than trusted blindly: 886 of 4526 (19.6%) matched their own real sibling resource within the same matched service group (326 exact token-set matches, 560 high-overlap matches), higher than the assumed 14%. Three real bugs were found and fixed during verification before trusting any output: a pluralization bug that mis-stripped words like responses/response into respons; a version-collapsing bug that let apigatewayv2 data sources match v1 resources instead of the correct v2 sibling; and a path-classification bug (recurring the same data/ directory-truncation quirk found earlier for AWS::DataZone/DataPipeline/DataBrew/DataSync/DataExchange resources) that wrongly excluded 2 real sibling candidates from consideration. 3640 fresh-authored orphans, individually written by real AWS service family (EC2, SageMaker, Bedrock, Connect, Cognito, IAM, and roughly 250 more services total), batched in 25 groups of ~150 for consistency.

intros.sourcing_notes: Batch 1 of the AWS CFN corpus (indices 0-96 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_access_analyzer_analyzer through aws_app_test_test_case). 57 of 97 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept (IAM Access Analyzer, AWS Private CA, Bedrock AgentCore Agent Registry, CloudWatch AIOps investigation groups, Amazon MQ brokers, AWS Amplify Hosting, Amplify UIBuilder, Amazon API Gateway REST APIs resources/stages/usage plans, AppConfig's full application/environment/deployment/experimentation surface, Amazon AppFlow, AppIntegrations, App Mesh's core mesh/node/router/service components, App Runner, WorkSpaces Applications (the renamed Amazon AppStream 2.0), AppSync GraphQL APIs and Events, and AWS Mainframe Modernization Application Testing). 40 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service (a usage-plan key against its usage plan, a v2 API Gateway sub-resource against the v2 API concept, an AppStream fleet/stack/entitlement association against the resource it associates, an AppSync API key or domain name against the GraphQL API it authorizes or fronts), the same parent-concept pattern proven across the prior five providers, most densely in this batch across API Gateway v1/v2's many sub-resources. 0 genuine skips: every one of the 97 real overview or reference pages fetched returned substantive content. Two notable non-recency findings surfaced live rather than assumed: AWS App Mesh carries an end-of-support notice (discontinued September 30, 2026, in favor of Amazon ECS Service Connect) and AWS App Runner is no longer open to new customers, both real, current vendor-page facts folded into their own intros rather than written as if the services were in normal active growth. Amazon AppStream 2.0 was verified live to have been renamed Amazon WorkSpaces Applications, with a real, newly expanded concepts page (agent sessions, computer use, an MCP service for AI agents) alongside its original fleet/stack/image-builder/app-block model; directory_config and entitlement, absent from that renamed concepts page, were confirmed real and still documented via a second, more targeted search rather than being assumed stale or skipped, the same two-search minimum the ticket's own GCP rollout_plan precedent established. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 97 (aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_target).
